items.title: Can you record a decision when no action is ranked?
items.why: MP-158 ties an entry to "the exact action" shown, and the records do not say what happens with no action. This one answer covers a rules-and-models disagreement and an abstention, where the model declines to forecast. With labels off until thresholds are approved, the drawn rule also leaves the journal nearly empty at launch.
items.drawn_today: Proposed: a disagreement can be recorded, saved with both sides. An abstention cannot take a new entry. Past entries stand.

options.says: You can save an entry against the evidence on screen whenever no action is ranked, and the entry records why none was.
options.cost: MP-158 is reworded and the journal's abstention and no-label screens change. An entry on an abstained horizon has no forecast to score, so it may never get an outcome.
options.because: You act at your broker whether or not MP ranks anything, and a journal that opens only on a label stays empty until thresholds are approved. It gives up a strict one-to-one tie between entry and action.

options.label: Disagreement yes, abstention no
options.says: As drawn: a disagreement can be saved, an abstention cannot.
options.cost: No redraw, but the rule is hard to explain, and most rows have nothing to record against until labels exist.

options.label: Ranked action only
options.says: An entry needs a ranked action, exactly as MP-158 reads.
options.cost: The cleanest record, but the disagreement sheet goes, and decisions made in those moments are lost to the journal.

items.title: What makes a risk alert material or critical?
items.why: Settled: a daily brief plus alerts for material risk, quiet hours 22:00 to 07:00 with only approved critical exceptions, and risk alerts kept apart from incidents. Left: the conditions. No record sets a value, and you approve them. The 30% line on screen is illustrative.
items.drawn_today: One alert is drawn: US tech above a 30% line, marked Material and held by quiet hours. Admin reads no values proposed and no exceptions approved. No critical alert is drawn.

options.label: Your lines, no investment wake-ups
options.says: Material means a line you set is crossed on exposure, price move, volatility or an event flag. Critical covers security and service faults only, so investment alerts wait for 07:30.
options.cost: A sharp overnight fall waits for the brief. Each line still needs a value from you before build.
options.because: This is a long-term tool, and the story asks to be told promptly but not woken. It gives up an overnight warning.

options.label: Add one severe wake-up
options.says: The same, and one severe investment condition you define may break quiet hours.
options.cost: That condition needs defining, no record proposes one, and a critical alert must be drawn.

options.label: Exposure lines only
options.says: Only exposure lines alert at launch, and the other kinds wait.
options.cost: A price shock shows only in the next brief.

asked.question: What makes a risk alert material or critical, and is there a weekend brief?
asked.drawn: How often the owner is alerted and on what (gap CT-18); until answered, alerts use the proposed thresholds and are labelled proposed.

items.title: Is there a weekend brief?
items.why: Settled: a daily brief at 07:30 London. Weekend delivery was left undecided. Either way one state is still undrawn, and alerts held overnight need somewhere to land.
items.drawn_today: Not drawn. The story holds a skipped state waiting for this answer.

options.label: Weekdays only
options.says: No brief on Saturday or Sunday. Home says why, and held alerts land in your inbox at 07:30 (proposed).
options.cost: No weekend look at the week ahead, and the rule that held alerts arrive with the brief changes.
options.because: Markets are shut, so it would mostly repeat Friday on a long-term tool, and it saves Claude spend. It gives up a weekend look ahead.

options.label: Every day, lighter at weekends
options.says: A short brief each weekend morning that says which markets are closed.
options.cost: Claude writes on days with no new closes. Its extra cost is not modelled (unverified) and sits inside the £15 Claude share.

options.label: Weekend brief by code
options.says: Code writes a plain weekend brief from stored figures, with no Claude.
options.cost: Plainer words, labelled as written by code.
